items.content:

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2023 NBAE (Photo by Joe Murphy/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images	With the LeBron James era officially over, it is time to move on to the Luka era and all his new teammates with the cap space the Lakers have used this offseason.

While the Lakers may have assembled a new squad this summer, many of the players already had connections to one another, which could speed up the process of building chemistry.

Let’s take a look at those.

Walker KesslerWalker Kessler and Austin Reaves played together at the FIBA World Cup in 2023. Kessler has also played with Jared Vanderbilt for half a season in his rookie season.

Collin Sexton played with Kessler in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons, developing a great chemistry with one another.

Quentin GrimesQuentin Grimes has played with Luka Dončić in the season after the Finals run and hold each other in high regard as despite not playing together very long. JJ has a connection with Grimes as, prior to him becoming coach of the Lakers, the pair worked out with JJ showing the process of being a professional.

Sandro MamukelashviliLuka has already reached out to Mamu about the fit together and how that will work. Mamu also played in Europe with Virtus Bologna while Luka was with Real Madrid.

Collin SextonHe has chemistry with Kessler from his Jazz days. Collin Sexton was on Redick’s podcast “The Old Man and the Three.”

Jaden HardyJaden Hardy played with Luka for two-and-a-half seasons with the Mavericks and was even part of the 2023-24 Finals run.

Ziare Williams He has chemistry with Bronny James from Sierra Canyon High School. He has also played with Jake LaRavia with the Memphis Grizzlies in his early years.

Kevon LooneyHe doesn’t have any chemistry with any of the current players on the roster, but he has lots of experience with ex-Lakers or soon-to-be Lakers in the following seasons with D’Angelo Russell, Dennis Schröder, Juan Toscano- Anderson, Quinn Cook, and JaVale McGee.

Matisse ThybulleMatisse Thybulle doesn’t have any connections to current players on the roster, but during his time in Portland, he played with players who have played in Los Angeles. Those include Josh Hart, Shaquille Harrison, Skylar Mays, Gary Payton II and Cam Reddish, both prior to and after being on the Lakers. JJ Redick also talked with him on his podcast four years ago.

With these connections among themselves and with the Lakers franchise, it should help develop chemistry. And with Luka hosting a mini camp in Slovenia, it should help build even more bonds to start the 2026-2027 NBA seaso

items.title: Shaquille O'Neal weighs in on Caitlin Clark situation, calls hard fouls a rite of passage
items.content:
NBA Hall of Famer Shaquille O'Neal knows a thing or two about getting fouled. During his NBA career, O'Neal faced punishment from some of the meanest big men around. Due to his spotty free-throw ability, O'Neal often found himself subject to some pretty rough and obvious fouls from defenders. 

That makes O'Neal uniquely qualified — in his opinion, at least — to talk about Caitlin Clark's current situation in the WNBA. Clark has been the subject of some particularly hard fouls this season, causing all manner of people — whether qualified or not — to weigh in on how the WNBA should protect one of its biggest stars. 

O'Neal doesn't see it that way, though. To O'Neal, what Clark is facing is something all the greats have endured early in their careers. During an interview with CNBC, O'Neal said all the hard fouls and rough treatment against Clark are "rites of passage" talented players have to overcome. 

"All the greats have to go through what we call rites of passage. She's a fabulous player, but we're not giving you anything, ever. You have to earn it," O'Neal said. "So for her, she needs to toughen up, take those licks, and show them that, 'These licks don't bother me.'"

That's not a surprising take from O'Neal, who — through previous comments — has made it clear he values toughness and sees hard fouls as a part of the game. That's probably due to the era in which O'Neal came up in the NBA. In the early '90s, the game was more physical. Chicago Bulls legend Michael Jordan, famously, took beatings from the Detroit Pistons in the playoffs early in his career, to the point where the Bulls had to bring in enforcers in free agency to retaliate and keep Jordan safe. 

While the NBA has cleaned up some of that, the WNBA still has some work to do. The league's officials have come under heavy criticism in recent seasons, with Clark expressing this year that she believes the refs need to be better.

She has her reasons for feeling that way. Clark has been involved in some rough plays since she entered the WNBA. As a rookie, she was involved in a particularly rough shoulder check from then-Chicago Sky guard Chennedy Carter. This season, Clark was on the receiving end of another flagrant foul after Alyssa Thomas appeared to push off Clark's throat after a play. 

When asked about the situation, Clark pointed out she's far from the only WNBA player to be involved in those types of plays. Ultimately, she put the onus on the officials and the WNBA, saying,"The league's just got to do better protecting our players."

O'Neal doesn't necessarily see it that way, believing WNBA players will eventually "invite [Clark] in and give [Clark] the throne" if she can endure the punishment now. While things may play out that way, Clark's desire for the league to protect its players should probably carry more weight, as she's the one actually taking hits right now.
